text:
maya (infra): Heads up — product told us TitanFrost will start receiving external traffic on Tue 07:00 UTC. They expect a steady ramp to ~650k tokens/sec globally within 2 hours.

kevin (infra): 650k tps global — that's material. Any regional breakdown?

sophie (capacity): PX sent a breakdown: us-east ~240k tps, eu-west ~280k tps, ap-south ~80k tps, other ~50k tps. These are peak sustained for ~3h during rollout.

liam (sre): Quick calc: with our current serving profile TitanFrost (32k context, flash-quant) needs ~140 tokens/sec per GPU for p95 < 150ms with batching. So 650k / 140 ≈ 464 GPUs.

kevin (infra): Oof. With autoscaling inefficiencies and headroom, call it 550 GPUs to hit SLOs during peak. That matches my rough estimate.

maya (infra): Baseline plan from ops-forecast-bot: recommend reserving 600 GPUs for 6h on rollout day (pre-warm + buffer). That is 600 * 6 = 3600 GPU-hours reserved.

ops-forecast-bot: projected_gpu_hours: 3600; projected_peak_gpus: 600; projected_cost_delta: $42k (spot + burst premium estimate).

kevin (infra): We should explore two mitigations: 1) aggressive KV/prefix caching to reduce token load by ~20% for common prompts, 2) a canary at 5% traffic routed to a lower-latency quantized variant.

sophie (capacity): If caching reduces load 20%, GPU need drops from 464 -> ~372 raw, with headroom ~440. That would save ~160 GPUs at peak. Worth it.

liam (sre): Network constraints: eu-west point of presence has only 280 GPUs free in our reserved pool that day (after other commitments). If eu-west hits 280 but expects 280k tps -> that's a deficit. We'll need cross-region routing to us-east for overflow which adds ~12–20ms latency for affected requests.

maya (infra): Product asked for latency impact estimate if overflow routed to us-east. liam, can you quantify p95 increase?

liam (sre): Rough: cross-region adds ~15ms median, p95 + ~25ms. For sensitive low-latency SLAs we'd breach 200ms p95. Should only route non-critical routes.

kevin (infra): Concrete ops items:
- pre-warm 20% capacity (120 GPUs) 1h before rollout to prime KV caches and kernels
- enable aggressive KV prefix caching for TitanFrost (config below)
- deploy canary at 5% to quantized variant QF-1 for fallback
- reserve 600 GPUs for 6h (ops to negotiate with cloud)

maya (infra): KV config snippet (will push to infra repo):
```yaml
model: TitanFrost
cache:
  prefix_cache: enabled
  ttl: 12h
  hot_keys: auto
  warmup: true
```

kevin (infra): Autoscale policy draft (will add to rollout):
```json
{"policy":"step","steps":[{"utilization":0.6,"add_gpus":50},{"utilization":0.8,"add_gpus":100},{"utilization":0.95,"add_gpus":200}],"cooldown_s":120}
```

ops-forecast-bot: cost_estimate_breakdown: ["reserved_prewarm: $8,400","on_demand_peak_burst: $25,600","data_transfer & cross-region: $8,000"]

sophie (capacity): If product can accept a slower ramp (2x longer), peak demand estimates drop ~30% — that could cut peak GPUs by ~150. Ask them to smooth rollout.

maya (infra): Action — @kevin to coordinate reserve purchase + autoscale landing by EOD today. @liam to draft cross-region fallback rules (only for non-SLA routes). @sophie to confirm caching knobs with devex.

kevin (infra): I'll open the reservation ticket and ping cloud ops. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-9321

liam (sre): Draft fallback rules: route overflow only for routes tagged `non-critical` AND response_time_estimate > 120ms. Add rollout flag `titanfrost.allow-overflow=true`.

maya (infra): If anyone sees alternate numbers or a better kernel/quantization knob that reduces tokens/sec per GPU, shout now.

kevin (infra): One more note — model warmup: we should run a synthetic warmup script for 30 minutes to populate KV and compilation caches. Command: `tools/warmup.sh --model TitanFrost --qf QF-1 --duration 30m --rate 5000`

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: titanfrost-canary -> 5% traffic at 2026-05-12T07:00:00Z

maya (infra): OK. We'll reconvene Tue 06:00 UTC for final go/no-go. For the thread: summary + APs posted to the rollout doc.

ops-forecast-bot: summary: peak 650k tps, proj peak gpus 464 raw (550 with headroom), recommend reserve 600 GPUs 6h, projected cost +$42k, mitigations: caching, canary QF-1, pre-warm 20%, staggered ramp requested.
